vignette.name: ILDA Files and ILDA Interface
vignette.h1: ILDA, ILDA Files and ILDA Interface"
vignette.p:
ILDA is the acronym for the International Laser Display Association, a non profit organisation that develops and releases standards for show laser control. Among others these are:
Laser proctor standards
The ILDA interface, a physical connector and a protocol to control laser projectors.
The ILDA file format to exchange image and animation data between devices. Often referred to as Ilda Files or ild files - due to the file extension .ild
You can find detailed information about the technical standards on the ILDA website: https://www.ilda.com/technical.htm

Legal Note: In the context of this packages (e.g as part of an object name) the acronym ILDA usually refers to the ILDA file format for is used as an abbreviation for the term Ilda File. It does not apply that any work is approved or released by the International Laser Display Association.

An ILDA interface uses a DB-25 connector. It is an analog interface where different pins control different aspects of the the laser projector (for example color values or X/Y position of the beam) by varying the voltage on the related pins.

For more information you can refer to the The ILDA Standard Projector specification here: https://www.ilda.com/resources/StandardsDocs/ILDA_ISP99_rev002.pdf
As it is an analog interface it does not allow to address various laser projectors, though some devices allow daisy chaining various projectors to use the same control signal.
An ILDA file (or .ild file) is a binary file that describes the movements an colors of the laser projector's beam.

It consists of a sequences of so-called frames or sections. One frame can either contain information about an ‘image’ - meaning I instructions for the laser projector how to move, or a definition of a color pallet - a list of color values associated with color indices.

A frame or section consists of two parts:
The Header, describing the frame
The Data Section (Data Records)
Source: ILDA Image Data Transfer Format Specification
Among other information the header describes what format the Data Section is using and how long it is. There are 5 possible formats:
The following Data Set describes the movement and the color of the laser beam using X, Y and Z coordinates and indices of colours from the color pallet.
The following Data Set describes the movement and the color of the laser beam using X and Y coordinates and indices of colours from the color pallet.
The following Data Set describes a custom color pallet to be used instead of the standard color pallet.
The following Data Set describes the movement and the color of the laser beam using X ,Y and Z coordinates and describes the color with separate values for red, green, and blue.
The following Data Set describes the movement and the color of the laser beam using X and Y coordinates and describes the color with separate values for red, green, and blue.
Objects in the Jam Package that deal with ILDA files will ignore frames/sections describing color pallets (FORMAT 2).

can handle all frame formats describing laser beam animations:
FORMAT 0 - 2D Coordinates with Indexed Color
FORMAT 1 - 2D Coordinates with Indexed Color
FORMAT 4 - 3D Coordinates with True Color
FORMAT 5 - 2D Coordinates with True Color

will always create ILDA files using FORMAT 5 frames (2D Coordinates with True Color).
Frames imported from an ILDA file will be converted to FORMAT 5 (flattened to 2D and indexed colors will be converted to true colors using the ILDA standard pallet).
